units.text: INT. ABANDONED CONSERVATORY - GLASSHOUSE - DAY
Dead palms.
Cracked panes.
A wrought-iron table in the center, set for tea.
INSPECTOR CLEMENTINE PRYCE (50s, tailored suit, kid gloves) pours from a silver pot.
Across from her sits SIR ALDOUS WREN (70s, cravat, a cane with a silver head), perfectly composed.
Sugar, Sir Aldous?
units.name: CLEMENTINE

units.text: Two, Inspector. As always.
units.name: ALDOUS

units.text: She drops two cubes into his cup.
He stirs, lifts it, and smiles.
You've grown quiet, my dear Clementine.
units.name: ALDOUS

units.text: I'm listening to the glass. It still sings in the wind.
units.name: CLEMENTINE

units.text: It sang the night my brother died.
units.name: ALDOUS

units.text: She sets down the pot very gently.
Her gloved hand rests on the table.
You were here that night, Aldous.
units.name: CLEMENTINE

units.text: I was in London.
units.name: ALDOUS

units.text: Your cuff, Sir Aldous. There's a leaf on it.
units.name: CLEMENTINE

units.text: He glances down.
A single pale frond, the kind that grows only in this room, clings to the cloth.
His smile does not move, but his fingers tighten on the cup.
Clementine, my dear. You were always the clever one.
units.name: ALDOUS

units.text: And you, Aldous, were always the early riser.
units.name: CLEMENTINE

units.text: She raises a hand.
Beyond the glass, two constables step from the hedges, and he sets the cup down without a sound.
